items.q: I don’t have time for anything this week — I’m too ___.
I ___ my sister every evening on my phone.
She writes a ___ about life with two small children.
I like to ___ time with my relatives at the weekend.

sub.en: Look at the questions. What comes between the question word and the main verb?

items.why: Question word + auxiliary + subject + verb. The auxiliary carries the tense, so the main verb stays in its base form.

items.q: What kind of music ___ you listen to?
What time ___ you go to bed last night?
How long ___ you lived in this city?
items.why: RECYCLED from Elementary: how long + present perfect, because the situation is still true.
With be there is no auxiliary — be itself moves in front of the subject.

items.q: How much time ___ you spend on your phone?

items.why: When the question word IS the subject, there is no auxiliary: Who lives here? not Who does live here?

acts.title: Three answers to the same six questions
text: We asked three people the same six questions. Here is what came back.

AIGUL, 31, Almaty. “Where do I live? In a flat near the centre — I’ve lived there for four years. What do I do? I’m a night nurse, so my week looks strange to everybody else. How often am I late? Never. In my job you can’t be. When did I last have fun? On Sunday. My sister came over and we talked until two in the morning.”

MARAT, 44, Taraz. “I run a small farm, and I’ve done it since my father stopped. Who do I live with? My wife, our two children and, in the summer, about nine relatives. How much time do I spend on my phone? Almost none — there isn’t any signal in the fields. What did I do at the weekend? I worked. I always work at the weekend.”

DANA, 26, Astana. “I’m a freelancer, so I choose my own hours and then fill every one of them. I write a blog about it. Do I enjoy going to museums? Honestly, no — I say yes and then I text an hour later to cancel. That’s a bad habit and I know it. How long have I worked for myself? Two years. Would I go back? No.”

items.s: Aigul has lived in her flat for four years.
Aigul is often late for work.
Marat took over the farm from his father.
Marat spends a lot of time on his phone.

write.q: Write six questions you would ask somebody you have just met. Use a present question, a past question, a “how long” question with the present perfect, a question with be, and one where the question word is the subject.
write.model: Where do you live? What do you do? How long have you worked there? Who lives with you? Are you busy this week? What did you do at the weekend? — and my favourite: When did you last have fun?

speak.q: Ask five of your questions out loud, then answer all five about yourself.
speak.model: Where do you live? — I live in Almaty, near the centre. How long have you lived there? — For about four years. What did you do at the weekend? — I saw my sister and we talked until two in the morning.
